title: Accessible, uncertainty-aware assembly of complex genomes

concept.text: The proposed innovation is a practical way to reconstruct complex genomes from sequencing reads while making uncertainty visible. It would recover long chromosome sequences and distinguish the related chromosome copies inherited from different parents, or the multiple copies present in polyploid organisms. Where the measurements cannot determine a single structure, it would preserve the ambiguity and identify additional measurements that could resolve it.

Genome assembly becomes difficult when repeated sequences look almost identical, related chromosome copies are hard to distinguish, sequencing coverage is uneven, or errors recur in the reads. The supplied hifiasm (ONT) study documents these problems through repeat and haplotype confusion, coverage-sensitive performance and unresolved repetitive regions. It also demonstrates substantial progress toward assembling genomes with standard nanopore simplex reads and CPU-based computation.

The conceptual limit is informational: if different genome structures produce indistinguishable observations, an algorithm cannot guarantee which one is correct from those observations alone. This is reasoning from the stated premise, rather than a theorem established by the supplied study. The proposed advance therefore combines efficient reconstruction where the evidence permits it with explicit alternatives where it does not. Broad accessibility, reliable phasing across complex genomes and useful uncertainty reporting together define the ambition; the supplied evidence does not establish that this combination has been achieved.

significance.text: A substantial reduction in sequencing, sample-preparation, computational and expertise requirements could allow many more biodiversity and medical research projects to obtain detailed assemblies. The supplied study identifies practical barriers to ultra-long sequencing that limit its use with clinical specimens and biodiversity samples. Its standard-read approach provides a concrete route toward lowering some of those barriers.

More complete reconstruction of repeats, structural variation and separate chromosome copies would improve access to genomic regions that fragmented or collapsed assemblies can obscure. The study's reconstruction of challenging medically relevant genes, including comparisons with the same-individual HG002 reference, grounds the connection to medical research. These examples demonstrate useful assembly capability within the tested scope; they do not establish general clinical benefit.

As a conditional synthesis, the revolutionary potential lies in making accurate, reliably phased assembly routine across diverse difficult genomes. This could broaden comparative genomics, improve investigation of complex variation and make better genomic inputs available to downstream discovery systems. Uncertainty reporting could also prevent unsupported structures from being treated as facts and direct limited sequencing budgets toward the measurements most likely to help.

The impact has important boundaries. High-quality assemblies already exist, and an incremental improvement to an assembler alone would not establish the proposed transformation. Cheaper assembly does not automatically deliver biological interpretation, causal explanations or clinically validated decisions. Those downstream benefits would require additional methods and evidence, while specimens with inadequate or uninformative measurements could remain unresolved.

missing_breakthrough.text: The unsolved capability is to combine accurate reconstruction, dependable separation of chromosome copies, practical resource requirements and informative uncertainty reporting across a broad range of complex genomes. The supplied study advances accessible near-telomere-to-telomere assembly, but it does not demonstrate broad empirical performance in polyploids or calibrated reporting of alternative genome structures.

Concrete barriers include distinguishing highly similar repeat copies and haplotypes, avoiding recurrent sequencing errors during read correction, and retaining enough useful evidence when coverage is limited. In the supplied experiments, most remaining human assembly gaps clustered in repetitive regions, homopolymer errors remained, and lower coverage was associated with poorer tomato assembly. Solving these problems requires improvements in both the measurements and the computational treatment of them.

Phasing adds a separate challenge: producing two assemblies does not by itself establish that each consistently represents one parental chromosome set. The study's ONT-only dual assemblies were partially phased, while fully phased diploid assembly required additional parental or Hi-C data. Methods that reason about more than two copies are relevant to polyploid assembly, but that algorithmic rationale does not substitute for broad empirical validation in polyploid species.

A proposed uncertainty-aware system would also need to distinguish missing information from algorithmic failure, express competing structures in a usable form, and connect unresolved choices to specific additional measurements. Reliable confidence estimates would need validation against independent evidence. Improving runtime cannot recover information absent from the reads, and resolving every ambiguity may require auxiliary sequencing whose cost must be included in any accessibility claim.

current_state.text: Cheng and colleagues' supplied 2026 study, “Efficient near-telomere-to-telomere assembly of nanopore simplex reads,” reports that hifiasm (ONT) can assemble standard nanopore simplex reads into near-telomere-to-telomere genomes without requiring ultra-long sequencing in that approach. Standard-simplex experiments included seven human samples and reconstructed multiple gapless chromosomes. Near-telomere-to-telomere describes substantial completeness; it does not mean that every tested genome was completely resolved.

The reviewed extraction of Table 1 reports hifiasm assembly times of 8.4–15.0 hours, compared with 86.7–126.7 hours for Verkko + HERRO in three trio comparisons. Hifiasm assembled directly from raw reads using CPUs, reducing assembly time and GPU requirements relative to that tested workflow. These measurements support a computational advantage in the reported comparisons; they do not establish superiority over every contemporary method or a corresponding reduction in the total cost of sequencing, auxiliary data and analysis.

Important limitations remained. Standard-read assemblies left difficult repetitive regions unresolved, most remaining human gaps clustered within repeats, and homopolymer errors persisted. ONT-only dual assemblies were partially phased; fully phased diploid assemblies required additional parental or Hi-C information. The article's discussion of failures in highly heterozygous regions concerned earlier consensus-first workflows and should not be read as a directly demonstrated hifiasm-specific failure in those regions.

The research record gives a publication date of February 4, 2026, and DOI 10.1038/s41586-026-10105-6. The supplied review notes that the artifact retains an online-publication-date placeholder, so the exact publication day was not independently confirmed. The review treated the available article content as partial: article and methods text through reporting materials was available, but graphical figures and some extended-data table values were absent from the extraction. The conclusions above rely on the reported prose and available table extraction rather than those missing values.

The supplied materials contain no freshness search record establishing whether later work superseded these findings or what the complete frontier was as of November 1, 2026. They also do not demonstrate the proposed combination of broad polyploid performance, calibrated ambiguity reporting and substantial total-cost savings. These are limits of the available evidence, not evidence that the documented results are false.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed demonstration: evaluate the system across independently selected diploid and polyploid species with difficult repeats and varied genome complexity. Predefine thresholds for sequence accuracy, structural correctness, completeness, phasing and resource use, together with what will count as a substantial practical improvement. These would be evaluation choices for this proposal, not established consensus standards.
completion_criteria.label: Diploid and polyploid evaluations predefine performance and practical improvement thresholds

completion_criteria.text: Validate difficult regions with independent measurements and assess chromosome-copy separation explicitly, rather than treating long contiguous sequences as sufficient proof of correctness. The supplied study's use of reference-based and reference-free evaluation, its same-individual HG002 comparisons and its distinction between partial and full phasing motivate these separate checks. Any proposed assessment should account for uncertainty or incompleteness in its validation data as well.
completion_criteria.label: Independent validation assesses difficult regions and chromosome-copy separation with uncertainty

completion_criteria.text: Proposed uncertainty demonstration: require the system to report unresolved structures and, where feasible, competing alternatives instead of forcing a single answer. Test whether reported confidence corresponds to observed correctness on independently resolved cases. For selected ambiguous regions, obtain the recommended additional measurements and assess whether they resolve the predicted uncertainty. A useful result would distinguish uncertainty that the existing evidence cannot resolve from errors that better inference can correct.
completion_criteria.label: Reported assembly uncertainty is calibrated and tested with additional measurements

completion_criteria.text: Proposed accessibility and reproducibility demonstration: report all required read types, sequencing coverage, sample-preparation requirements, parental or Hi-C inputs, computing hardware, memory, runtime, manual intervention and total cost or effort. Compare against contemporary methods under transparent conditions, and make data, software versions, settings and evaluation procedures available so independent groups can reproduce the results. Savings in one computational stage should be assessed alongside any costs transferred to auxiliary measurements or expert work.
completion_criteria.label: Full resource accounting and transparent comparisons enable independent reproduction

completion_criteria.text: A convincing outcome would establish a clearly bounded range of genomes and input conditions in which the system meets its predefined criteria, while documenting failures and unresolved regions. Finite tests can establish demonstrated breadth across the selected cases; they cannot establish literal universality, guaranteed perfect assembly or a universal linear-time solution. Practical completion would include a reliable way to recognize and communicate the system's boundaries.
completion_criteria.label: Demonstrated genome and input boundaries include failures and unresolved regions

related_concepts.text: Within the supplied roster, BIF-12, “Strain-resolved discovery and functional profiling of microbial communities,” has the closest reconstruction overlap: both must distinguish related sequences and manage ambiguity. BIF-11 focuses on assembling complex genomes and their chromosome copies; BIF-12 additionally concerns mixtures of organisms, strain separation and community functional profiling. Existing telomere-to-telomere assembly, haplotype phasing, repeat resolution and assembly-quality assessment are direct technical foundations for BIF-11.

BIF-01, “A predictive decoder for the regulatory genome,” and BIF-06, “A general decoder for unknown gene and protein functions,” could use better assembled sequence as input, but address what that sequence does. BIF-02, “Predictive molecular dynamics from biological sequence,” and BIF-09, “Proteome-scale prediction of molecular interactions and affinities,” concern molecular behavior and interactions. Accurate reconstruction can improve their inputs without supplying their missing predictive capabilities.

BIF-03, “A transferable, predictive virtual cell,” BIF-04, “General reconstruction of causal cellular networks,” BIF-07, “Computational reconstruction of organism-scale molecular maps,” and BIF-08, “Reliable reconstruction and forecasting of single-cell fates,” address cellular or organismal organization, causality and dynamics. BIF-11 could provide a more reliable genomic foundation, but assembling chromosomes does not by itself reconstruct cellular networks, spatial molecular maps or cell-fate trajectories.

BIF-05, “Computer-aided design of functional whole genomes,” and BIF-13, “Predictive design of functional genetic circuits and pathways,” concern designing biological systems. BIF-11 could help verify the sequence and structure of constructed material, while leaving functional design and performance prediction as distinct challenges. BIF-10, “A broadly capable autonomous bioinformatics discovery system,” could incorporate assembly as one capability, but would additionally require broader autonomous analysis and discovery. These roster relationships are conceptual synthesis from the supplied titles, not findings demonstrated by the assembly study.

change_log.change: Preserved BIF-11's identity and integrated accessible reconstruction, chromosome-copy separation and explicit ambiguity into one concept.
change_log.reason: The proposed innovation combines practical assembly with uncertainty awareness; evidence for progress in one component does not establish completion of the whole.

change_log.change: Specified the computational comparison as hifiasm versus the tested Verkko + HERRO workflow and retained the reported runtime ranges.
change_log.reason: The supplied review supports 8.4–15.0 versus 86.7–126.7 hours in three trio comparisons, rather than a claim of universal superiority or total-pipeline savings.

change_log.change: Separated near-telomere-to-telomere reconstruction, gapless chromosomes, partial phasing and fully phased diploid assembly.
change_log.reason: These are different achievements, and fully phased diploid assembly required additional parental or Hi-C data in the supplied study.

change_log.change: Corrected attribution of highly heterozygous-region failures and retained documented repeat, coverage and homopolymer limitations.
change_log.reason: The heterozygosity discussion concerned earlier consensus-first workflows; residual repetitive gaps and homopolymer errors were directly documented for the reported assemblies.

change_log.change: Expanded completion criteria with predefined thresholds, independent validation, uncertainty testing, reproducibility and full resource accounting.
change_log.reason: These additions make qualitative goals testable while preserving their status as proposals rather than published standards.

change_log.change: Preserved the conditional medical and biodiversity significance while distinguishing assembly from interpretation and clinical validation.
change_log.reason: The evidence supports a route toward broader research access, but does not establish downstream clinical benefit.

change_log.change: Included publication-date uncertainty, partial extraction and the missing freshness record.
change_log.reason: These limitations affect interpretation and temporal scope without invalidating the documented study results.

change_log.change: Explained relationships to every other supplied roster entry without merging their objectives.
change_log.reason: Assembly can support downstream prediction, design and discovery while remaining a distinct capability.

unresolved_issues: The exact publication day remains unconfirmed because the research date and the artifact's online-date placeholder were not reconciled.
No supplied freshness record establishes whether later work superseded these results or defines the full frontier as of November 1, 2026.
Graphical figures and some extended-data table values were unavailable in the reviewed extraction, limiting assessment of those details.
Broad empirical performance across complex polyploid genomes is not established by the supplied study.
Calibrated uncertainty reporting, representation of competing structures and effective recommendations for additional measurements remain proposed capabilities.
Numerical thresholds for accessibility, accuracy, completeness, phasing and substantial total-cost improvement remain to be defined.
The scope of total practical savings remains unresolved once auxiliary sequencing, sample preparation, computing and expert intervention are included.

brief.title: Affordable DNA reconstruction with visible uncertainty
possible: Researchers could reconstruct a genome, an organism’s complete set of DNA, with fewer resources. They could recover long chromosome sequences, the DNA strands that carry genes, while keeping related copies separate, including in organisms with multiple copies.
When measurements leave several possible DNA structures, the system would preserve those alternatives and identify extra measurements that could settle the question.
why: More biodiversity and medical research projects could obtain detailed genomes. Reconstructing repeated DNA and keeping chromosome copies separate would expose genetic differences that fragmented or merged sequences can hide.
Visible uncertainty would help researchers avoid treating unsupported structures as facts. It could also direct limited sequencing budgets toward measurements most likely to resolve an ambiguity.

sources.who: Haoyu Cheng, Han Qu and colleagues
sources.showed: Their hifiasm software reconstructed chromosomes from end to end using standard nanopore sequencing, which reads individual DNA strands. It reduced computing demands compared with the tested alternatives.
sources.quote:
Compared with existing methods, hifiasm (ONT) reduces computational 
demands by an order of magnitude and reconstructs more chromosomes from 
telomere to telomere on the same datasets.
sources.cited_for: Standard sequencing can support more complete genomes with less computation.
sources.not_established: Broad performance in organisms with multiple chromosome copies, reliable uncertainty reporting and total practical savings remain unproven.

sources.showed: They developed a human genome benchmark that separates inherited chromosome copies and identifies regions of low confidence. Most of its sequence had no detectable errors.
sources.cited_for: Independent benchmarks can assess reconstruction quality while identifying regions that remain uncertain.
sources.not_established: A detailed human benchmark does not establish broad assembly performance or reliable confidence estimates across complex genomes.

sources.showed: This preprint presents pHapCompass, software that estimates alternative ways to assign DNA variants to chromosome copies. Tests reported competitive accuracy and useful uncertainty estimates, largely using simulated genomes.
sources.quote:
Lastly, we produce the first assembly of
an allo-octoploid Strawberry chromosome.
sources.cited_for: Uncertainty about chromosome-copy assignment can be represented and measured.
sources.not_established: These results do not establish affordable, complete genome reconstruction across diverse organisms with multiple chromosome copies.

sources.who: Haoyu Cheng, Erich D. Jarvis and colleagues
sources.showed: This preprint combined accurate DNA reads with measurements of DNA contacts inside cells. It separated inherited chromosome copies without sequencing parents, with results comparable to approaches using family data.
sources.quote:
Applied to human and other vertebrate samples, our algorithm consistently outperforms existing
single-sample assembly pipelines and generates assemblies of comparable quality to the best pedigree-based assemblies.
sources.cited_for: Additional measurements can separate inherited chromosome copies without parental sequencing.
sources.not_established: The approach still requires extra contact measurements and does not establish reliable performance across genomes with more chromosome copies.

shown: Cheng and colleagues’ hifiasm reconstructed multiple gapless chromosomes using standard nanopore reads across seven human samples. It ran on conventional processors. Fully separating inherited chromosome sets still required parental data or measurements of DNA contacts.

Hosseini and colleagues’ pHapCompass preprint tackles uncertainty about chromosome-copy assignment. Its tests, largely on simulated genomes, reported competitive accuracy and useful confidence estimates.
missing: No system has demonstrated accurate reconstruction, dependable chromosome-copy separation and useful uncertainty reporting across diverse complex genomes.
Confidence estimates still need independent tests, including whether recommended extra measurements resolve the predicted ambiguities.
Substantial savings still need demonstration after counting sequencing, sample preparation, computing and expert effort.

milestones.label: Diverse genome tests meet predefined performance and resource thresholds
milestones.explanation: Tests would have to meet predefined accuracy, completeness, chromosome-copy separation and resource thresholds across independently selected complex genomes. This would establish meaningful practical improvement.

milestones.label: Independent measurements validate difficult regions and chromosome-copy separation
milestones.explanation: Independent measurements would have to confirm difficult sequences and chromosome-copy separation, accounting for their own uncertainty. This would establish correctness beyond the length of reconstructed DNA.

milestones.label: Confidence predicts correctness, and extra measurements resolve ambiguities
milestones.explanation: Reported alternatives and confidence would have to match independently resolved cases, and recommended measurements would have to resolve selected ambiguities. This would make uncertainty useful.

milestones.label: Full resource comparisons support independent reproduction
milestones.explanation: Transparent comparisons would have to count all measurements, preparation, computing and expert work, with enough detail for independent reproduction. This would establish whether savings hold across the whole process.

milestones.label: Demonstrated operating boundaries include failures and unresolved regions
milestones.explanation: Tests would have to establish which genomes and inputs meet the criteria, while documenting failures and unresolved regions. This would let researchers recognize and communicate the system’s limits.

uncertain: How well will performance extend across diverse organisms with multiple chromosome copies?
What thresholds should count as sufficiently accurate, complete and affordable?
When observations fit competing structures equally well, which additional measurements can distinguish them at a practical cost?

page.title: Haplotype-resolved genome assembly with uncertainty quantification
page.definition: Haplotype-resolved assembly reconstructs each chromosome copy separately from DNA reads and assigns probabilities to unresolved alternatives, with lower total workflow cost than a matched method. It covers diploids (two chromosome sets), autopolyploids (extra sets from one species) and allopolyploids (sets from different species).

goal.need: In the HG002 benchmark study, assembly-based analysis recovered 2–7% more sequence than reference-based variant calling. Nevertheless, 3,172 regions spanning 38.8 Mb of its 6.0 Gb diploid assembly remained low confidence. Sample requirements also affect access: the hifiasm study reports that human ultra-long nanopore sequencing needs about 40 times the DNA input of the standard protocol.

figures.caption: Assembly wall time for three human trio comparisons, reported on 4 February 2026.
figures.note: Standard nanopore simplex reads were supplemented with parental phasing data. Hardware differed: hifiasm used 64 CPUs; Verkko + HERRO used servers with more than 64 CPUs and multiple GPUs. These timings do not establish total workflow costs.

completion.title: Independent replication combines phased complete assemblies, calibrated alternatives and lower total cost.
completion.criterion: An independent laboratory reproduces, for a real genome in each listed class, a workflow meeting the chromosome-completeness, QV >60 and phasing tests below. Alternative structures and phase assignments meet calibration endpoints specified in a published validation protocol using independent truth data. Total cost is lower than for a comparator meeting the same sequence and phasing tests, counting DNA extraction, library preparation, all sequencing and auxiliary data, computation and human curation. The validation protocol must set calibration bounds; no community-wide numerical bound was found.
completion.set_by: Technology Atlas; proposed composite demonstration, pending an externally published calibration protocol.
completion.basis: Searches of VGP and EBP assembly standards, NHGRI planning documents, GIAB benchmark papers and polyploid uncertainty protocols found no joint completion criterion. External documents supply sequence and phasing thresholds, but no acceptance bound combining calibrated alternatives and total cost. This proposal retains those assembly thresholds and requires independent validation and a measured cost reduction; its calibration component remains incompletely specified.

milestones.title: A genome reaches 1 Mb contig N50, chromosome-scale scaffolding and QV >40.
milestones.criterion: Meet EBP's sufficient-material reference standard: contig N50 at least 1 Mb, chromosome-scale scaffold N50, error rate <10^-4, false duplication <5%, and >90% each for k-mer completeness, chromosome assignment, conserved-gene completeness/single-copy status and transcript mapping. N50 is the length at which half the assembly lies in sequences that long or longer. Chromosome-scale contigs replace 1 Mb for smaller chromosomes; biological exceptions apply to duplicated polyploid genes. On 4 February 2026, hifiasm reported QV 47.5/47.1 for HG002's two trio-phased haplotypes (one donor); this alone does not establish every condition.
milestones.set_by: EBP Sequencing and Assembly Standards committee, Report on Assembly Standards version 7.0, agreed on 31 January 2026; sufficient-material category.

milestones.title: A haplotype assembler infers a probability distribution over chromosome-copy assignments.
milestones.criterion: Infer and sample a distribution over assignments of variants to chromosome copies while propagating uncertainty about read origin; phase probabilities follow sampled configuration frequencies. The 11 March 2026 pHapCompass preprint benchmarks 3,120 simulated read datasets, including diploid, autopolyploid and allopolyploid configurations. Experimental tests use one octoploid strawberry biosample, aggregated over seven chromosomes at 8× and 16× coverage. These are reference-aligned variant-phasing results; they establish neither gapless genome reconstruction nor independent probability calibration. The cited results are not peer reviewed.
milestones.set_by: pHapCompass developers, computational protocol in Methods and section 4.5; the criterion concerns inferred distributions, without a published calibration acceptance threshold.
milestones.threshold_quote: In both models, the probability of a phasing is proportional to the number of consistent FFBS samples.

milestones.title: A genome assembly exceeds QV50, contig NG50 10 Mb and phase-block NG50 1 Mb.
milestones.criterion: Meet the VGP-2020 continuity, phasing and base-accuracy thresholds: contig NG50 >10 Mb, scaffold NG50 equal to chromosome NG50, phase-block NG50 >1 Mb and QV >50 (error rate <10^-5). NG50 uses estimated genome length rather than assembled length. A 10 September 2021 preprint reports HG002 Hi-C hifiasm contig N50s of 57.6/44.9 Mb and haplotype Hamming errors of 0.89/0.99% (one donor). These measurements do not establish all four thresholds or either polyploid case; the cited version is not peer reviewed.
milestones.set_by: Vertebrate Genomes Project, Table 1, VGP-2020 continuity, base-accuracy and phasing rows. Thresholds occur in a table. Their original scope is vertebrate genomes about 1 Gb or larger; application to plant polyploids extends that scope.

milestones.title: A genome assembly is gapless at QV >60 with chromosome-scale phase-block NG50.
milestones.criterion: Meet EBP's T2T conditions in every haplotype: all telomeres where applicable, no sequence gaps and QV >60 (estimated base error rate <10^-6), plus VGP's Finished phase-block NG50 equal to chromosome NG50. In the 6 August 2026 HG002 paper (one donor), 99.35% of 6.0 Gb had no detected errors, but nine ribosomal-DNA gaps spanned 31.1 Mb. Its title therefore does not establish this milestone. The cited autopolyploid simulations and allopolyploid variant-phasing experiments do not establish it either.
milestones.set_by: EBP version 7.0 T2T definition, combined with the VGP Table 1 Finished phasing row. The VGP metric was proposed for vertebrate genomes about 1 Gb or larger; application to plant polyploids extends that scope.
milestones.threshold_quote: all telomere sequences (where applicable), the absence of sequence gaps and a QV greater than 60

not_found: No external document was found defining a joint pass criterion for complete phased assembly, calibrated alternatives and total workflow cost.
No numerical acceptance bound was found for independently calibrated structural and polyploid phasing probabilities; a published validation protocol remains necessary.
No opened study demonstrated the proposed combined completion test across real diploid, autopolyploid and allopolyploid genomes.
No externally set acceptance test was found for recommending additional measurements that resolve assembly alternatives.
